interest: 1944–45 debate over Japanese communism, plus 1943 tightening of local government and neighborhood associations.
overview: This file comprises two distinct U.S. government documents from mid-October 1944 classified under decimal file 894.00B (Bolshevism, Communism, and Subversive Activities in Japan). The first document is an internal State Department memorandum from Erle R. Dickover (Chief of the Division of Japanese Affairs) to Joseph C. Grew (Director of the Office of Far Eastern Affairs), analyzing an interview conducted in Yan'an (Yenan) by Foreign Service Officer John S. Service with Japanese Communist Party leader Susumu Okano (Sanzō Nosaka) and firmly opposing Service's recommendation that the United States extend 'sympathetic support' to Japanese Communists. The second document is a multi-page confidential intelligence translation issued on October 19, 1944, by the U.S. Navy's Office of the Chief of Naval Operations (Op-16-FF, Division of Naval Intelligence), translating an article from the June 23, 1943 issue of Shūhō (the official weekly bulletin of the Japanese Cabinet Board of Information) that details wartime structural reorganizations of Japan's prefectural, municipal, town, and village administrations designed to streamline local governance and tighten central wartime mobilization.

subfiles.about: An evaluation and critique of the Japanese Communist Party's postwar platform as reported by John S. Service from Yan'an, recommending against U.S. support for the party.
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, Chief, Division of Japanese Affairs
subfiles.summary: Dickover reviews Service's Yan'an interview with Okano (Nosaka). He finds parts of the program at odds with U.S. policy and rejects Service's call for sympathetic support of the Japanese Communist Party, which he says would alienate Japanese liberals.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Erle R. Dickover to Joseph C. Grew Regarding Japanese Communist Party Program and Report of John S. Service
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: A translation of an official Japanese Cabinet Board of Information question-and-answer article detailing wartime legislative revisions to municipal, town, village, and prefectural administration enacted in June 1943.
subfiles.from: Op-16-FF (Office of the Chief of Naval Operations, Division of Naval Intelligence)
subfiles.summary: This intelligence bulletin translates an extensive article from the June 23, 1943 issue of Shūhō, the official publication of the Japanese Cabinet Board of Information, outlining revisions to local governance laws aimed at maximizing efficiency for the Greater East Asia War. The reforms centralize executive control by requiring Imperial sanction or gubernatorial confirmation for the appointment and removal of mayors and village headmen, severely curtailing the budgetary, investigative, and procedural powers of local assemblies, and capping assembly sizes in major urban centers such as Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya. The measure also provides legal recognition and state integration for neighborhood and community associations (chōnai-kai and buraku-kai), establishes regional branch offices in rural counties, and incorporates Hokkaido and Karafuto (Sakhalin) more uniformly into standard domestic local administration.
subfiles.title: Office of Naval Intelligence Translation No. 69: 'Changes in Japanese Local Administration' (from Shūhō)
subfiles.to: Multiple recipients (including State Department, Cominch, CINCPAC, JICPOA, OSS, and MIS)
